name: Axiom Systems Cortical Bomb CB-1 'Leash'
description: A micro-explosive device designed to be implanted adjacent to a target's neural interface, detonating on receipt of a coded signal or upon detection of tampering. The CB-1 contains 0.5 grams of high-velocity explosive — insufficient to kill outright but precisely enough to destroy the neural interface and cause catastrophic brain damage. Axiom developed it as a compliance enforcement tool for high-risk assets — individuals who possess critical information or capabilities that must be denied to competitors if the asset defects or is captured. The existence of the CB-1 is officially denied, but the distinctive brain damage pattern it produces has been identified in enough autopsy reports to confirm its deployment.
specifications: explosive yield: 0.5g high-velocity micro-charge detonation trigger: Coded RF signal or tamper detection implant size: 3mm x 3mm x 1mm implant location: Adjacent to neural interface housing effect: Neural interface destruction + severe traumatic brain injury survival rate: approximately 40% with immediate medical intervention tamper detection: Accelerometer + magnetic field sensor RF trigger range: 500 meters from transmitter
story_hooks: A defecting corporate scientist begs for help removing a CB-1 from their skull — any neurosurgeon who attempts removal risks triggering the tamper detection, and the coded detonation signal could come at any time.

A batch of CB-1 implants has been discovered with a firmware vulnerability that allows the detonation code to be brute-forced — someone is quietly scanning for implanted individuals and building a kill list.

physical_description.visual_profile: A barely-visible surgical implant; when extracted or displayed, appears as a minuscule metallic wafer no larger than a grain of rice. Under magnification, reveals circuitry traces and a central charge cavity. Not typically seen intact — exists primarily as component parts scattered through neural tissue or as classified documentation.
physical_description.dimensions: 3mm length × 3mm width × 1mm thickness (implant core); transmission unit (if separate) approximately 12cm × 8cm × 4cm
physical_description.weight_description: Virtually weightless as implant; transmission unit is pocket-sized and lightweight, designed for concealment
physical_description.primary_material: Surgical-grade titanium casing, bio-compatible polymer isolation layer, copper trace circuitry, micro-charge core (proprietary explosive compound)
physical_description.finish: Mirror-polished titanium with iridescent biofilm layer from neural tissue contact; circuitry traces show in matte gold; charge cavity appears as dark void
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray with gold circuit traces; dark charcoal at detonation chamber. Transmission unit: matte black composite with subtle Axiom Systems silver branding
physical_description.grip_texture: N/A for implant (subcutaneous); transmission unit features rubberized non-slip polymer with recessed button interface
distinctive_features: Dual-sensor array: accelerometer + magnetic field detector etched into substrate
Central void cavity containing micro-charge (0.5g high-velocity explosive)
Bio-compatible polymer sheath with microperforations for neural signal passthrough
RF receiver coil wrapped around implant perimeter
Miniaturized capacitor bank for RF signal amplification
Failsafe detonator primed but dormant under normal conditions
Tissue scarring pattern around implant is diagnostically distinctive (classified autopsy indicator)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Axiom Systems logo stamped in 0.5mm font on transmission unit only; implant itself unmarked for deniability. Serial number encrypted in firmware
physical_description.condition_typical: As implant: pristine until detonation, then fragmented. As recovered evidence: partial charred fragments embedded in cortical matter, requiring forensic reconstruction. Transmission unit: kept in Faraday-lined case when not in use, shows minimal wear due to clandestine operational security
